related_questions.question: What is the survival rate for TCC cancer?

text_blocks.snippet: The survival rate for Transitional Cell Carcinoma (TCC), also known as Urothelial Carcinoma, varies significantly based on the cancer's stage and location. Early-stage, superficial TCC in the renal pelvis or ureter can have a survival rate of over 90%. However, if the cancer is deeply invasive or has spread to other parts of the body, the survival rate can drop to 15% or lower.
snippet_highlighted_words: Early-stage, superficial TCC in the renal pelvis or ureter can have a survival rate of over 90%

list.title: Renal Pelvis and Ureter:
list.snippet: More than 90% of patients with superficial tumors confined to the renal pelvis or ureter are curable.

list.title: Bladder Cancer:
list.snippet: The five-year survival rate for localized bladder cancer (confined to the bladder) is around 71%, while carcinoma in situ (abnormal cells in the lining) has a 97% survival rate.

list.title: Distant Metastases:
list.snippet: The survival rate for patients with tumors that have spread to other parts of the body is significantly lower, often 15% or lower.

list.title: Metastatic Bladder Cancer:
list.snippet: The five-year survival rate for metastatic bladder cancer is only around 8%.

list.title: Tumor grade and stage:
list.snippet: Higher-grade tumors and those that have invaded deeper into the tissue have a poorer prognosis.

list.title: Tumor location:
list.snippet: Tumors in the renal pelvis tend to have a better prognosis than those in the ureter.

list.title: Presence of other health problems:
list.snippet: Conditions like renal insufficiency or prior bladder cancer can also affect survival.
For patients with low-grade, low-stage TCC in the renal pelvis or ureter, five-year survival rates can approach 100% after conservative surgery.
For patients with high-grade, invasive TCC, survival rates can be as low as 20-30%.
In some studies, the five-year survival rate for patients with advanced bladder cancer has been reported to be as low as 9% for distant stage and 40% for regional stage.

text_blocks.snippet: In conclusion, while early-stage TCC has a high survival rate, the prognosis for advanced or metastatic TCC is much more challenging. Treatment options and survival outcomes vary greatly depending on the specific characteristics of the cancer and the individual patient.
